newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN DEBT PRICES SEE-SAW IN THIN VOLUMES.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN DEBT PRICES SEE-SAW IN THIN VOLUMES.

text.p: German Bunds and futures see-sawed through Thursday's session in a market dominated by currency movements and ruffled by market rumours.

After a subdued start, news of a 25 basis points interest rate rise in Britain helped Bunds higher as the mark gained against the pound, redcuding fears in Germany that the Bundesbank may tighten rates.
But Bunds lost ground again in afternoon trade as rumours -- swiftly denied by the German government -- that Chancellor Helmut Kohl was dead unsettled the market.
"We're getting into silly season," said one London-based trader. "The markets are looking for something to do and so this rumour about Kohl started going around."
By 1514 GMT, the September DTB Bund future was one basis point higher on the day at 102.01, but continually dipping in and out of negative ground.
Analysts said Bunds were likely to remain jumpy ahead of the Bundesbank's repo decision due by Tuesday.
One analyst noted a sharp rise in German call money rates to around 3.15 percent, saying this was a sign that some large players remain wary that the repo will rise at the next tender.

"Those major players in the domestic money market now causing the call money squeeze may of course be wrong about a repo rate rise next week, but it is conspicuous that their reserves strategy implies that expectation," he said.
In the cash market, the 10-year benchmark Bund was trading one tick higher at 102.35 for a bid yield of 5.674 percent by 1528 GMT.
The yield spread showed the German market sharply underperforming U.S. Treasuries, slimming to 60 basis points from around 65 basis points in late Wednesday trade.
